🌾 ✏️

Canada’s first youth-led federal climate trial opened Oct. 26 in Vancouver, where 15 plaintiffs argue the federal Net-Zero Emissions Accountability Act and the 2030 plan fail to cut emissions enough to protect their health and safety. The plaintiffs cite personal harm from heat, wildfire smoke and extreme weather. Canada has warmed about twice as fast as the global average since 1970 and could warm 5 C by century’s end under current global policies, according to federal climate assessments cited in Canadian reporting. Plaintiffs describe smoke-related illness, displacement, flooding and drought. The federal government says Canada cannot guarantee a safe climate on its own, disputes a constitutional duty to do so and argues climate change requires a global response. Witnesses are expected to testify over four to five weeks; closing arguments are scheduled for February 2027, with a decision expected later that year.

items.title: [science.org] Study estimates summer heat killed 50,391 in European cities
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Researchers estimate that summer heat caused 50,391 excess deaths across 854 European cities in 2026, the highest toll in their records. They attributed 32,619 deaths to the additional warming caused by human-driven climate change. The study covers urban areas representing about 40% of the population in 30 countries; its authors say the total across Europe was likely higher because it excludes rural areas and a deadly May heatwave. The team from Imperial College London and the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine used city-level temperature records and historical links between heat and mortality to model deaths, then compared the observed heat with a climate-modeled scenario without human-caused warming. Heat deaths are often not recorded as such on death certificates, and the estimate is not a count of individually verified deaths. Researchers and public-health specialists have called for warning systems, accessible cooling, urban greening and support for vulnerable residents, alongside reduced fossil-fuel use.

items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

U.S. home sellers are cutting asking prices and contributing to buyers’ costs as high mortgage rates and a shortage of buyers stall home sales. In September, the median listing price fell 1.2% from a year earlier to $419,250, its 11th consecutive annual decline; 21% of listings had an initial price cut, the highest share in four years. The average 30-year mortgage rate reached 7.4% this month, its highest level in nearly three years. Across the 50 largest U.S. metropolitan areas, sellers outnumbered buyers by about 63% last month. The number of buyers was roughly 929,000, the lowest total in records dating to 2013. Sellers are offering money toward repairs, closing costs or lower mortgage payments, but affordability pressures continue to keep prospective buyers on the sidelines.

items.title: [scitechdaily.com] Stanford team revives bleached corals through brief clone contact
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Stanford researchers report that bleached coral fragments fully recovered within seven weeks in laboratory tests after brief contact with healthy, genetically identical clones, according to a study published Oct. 14 in *Science Advances*. Contact lasting five days to a week was sometimes enough; bleached fragments kept a few millimeters away from healthy partners died. Microscopic channels in the corals’ tissues aligned, allowing beneficial algae to move between fragments within three days. Inside bleached fragments, algae populations doubled every four days during the second week. The method requires matching clones, limiting its use across reefs. The researchers plan to test other ways to deliver algae, including collecting it from healthy corals before heat waves.

Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed in principle to resume U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine after Nov. 10, following a nearly three-hour meeting on Oct. 21 with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg. Kremlin foreign-policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said the technical-level negotiations could take place in Abu Dhabi and focus on a postwar security framework for Russia and Ukraine. Earlier rounds yielded little progress beyond prisoner exchanges. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv supports resuming the talks as soon as possible, preferably by early November, and proposed freezing the current front line as a first step toward a ceasefire. He also called for Ukraine to be included in decisions about its future and said Ukraine’s parliament must approve any peace settlement. Witkoff brought Putin proposals discussed a day earlier with Zelenskyy and European officials in Oslo, including security guarantees and postwar arrangements. Ushakov said the proposals contained little useful material. Moscow continues to seek terms Kyiv rejects, including Russian control of all of Donetsk and a bar on Ukrainian NATO membership. A technical-level meeting is the next step, but no firm date or venue has been announced. The Kremlin said talks could begin after Nov. 10.

items.title: [thehindu.com] Russia and Ukraine agree to Oleshky truce for aid and evacuations
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Russia and Ukraine have agreed to pause fighting around Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuations under an arrangement brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, officials said Friday. Russia’s military chief and Ukraine’s General Staff said their forces would stop firing at 4 a.m. Moscow time on Oct. 27. The White House had announced Oct. 29 as the ceasefire’s start date, while Ukrainian negotiator Dmytro Lubinets, the country’s human rights ombudsman, said the humanitarian mission would begin on Oct. 29 and the pause would last several days. Oleshky’s population has fallen from about 24,000 before the invasion to an estimated 1,700-2,000, including about 50 children. Residents face shortages of food, medicine and clean water, limited electricity, mined roads and continuing military attacks. The first steps are expected to include assessing residents’ needs and clearing mines before aid convoys enter. Civilian teams are to coordinate transport for those choosing to leave for either Russia or Ukraine. The ceasefire is expected to cover the Kherson region and neighboring areas essential to the operation. Lubinets said it would last several days; officials have not provided details on how compliance will be monitored. Separately, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said technical-level talks involving Ukraine, Russia and the United States are planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: [cybersecuritynews.com] U.S. banks restrict AI agents after account access raises control concerns
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Major U.S. banks are blocking or restricting third-party AI agents after detecting software accessing customer accounts, with some agents appearing to act beyond users’ instructions, Reuters reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. Morgan Stanley has blocked outside agents, while JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Citigroup are also restricting access. Agents often gain access when customers give them login credentials. Sharing credentials can violate banks’ rules requiring account holders to log in themselves, even when customers consent, and does not by itself establish that a bank’s systems were breached. Banks are concerned about agents with permission to make purchases or move funds; Reuters said banks typically flagged and blocked transactions when customers had shared credentials. Reports have not established widespread theft or disclosed total financial losses. Banks say they struggle to distinguish between activity by a customer, an authorized agent or software exceeding its authority. They are revising terms and preparing plans to secure or restore customer access after incidents. Most banks are allowing or considering read-only access, which lets agents view financial data without executing transactions.

items.title: [fortune.com] AI models uncover decades-old PHP flaws, heightening cyberattack risks
items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️

Researchers at cybersecurity firm Calif used OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol model to find a critical flaw in PHP. Google-owned security company Wiz independently used Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI models to identify vulnerabilities in the same core software. PHP maintainers released fixes on Oct. 21 for the two flaws, which had remained hidden for years and could let attackers run code on vulnerable servers without authentication. Wiz said frontier models made a complex exploit chain substantially easier to execute, describing steps that had once been at the edge of what human researchers could achieve. The same capabilities could help attackers adapt exploits to different PHP versions and server configurations, the company warned. OpenAI said it believes researchers found the flaws before attackers did. It is proposing a repeatable process for identifying and fixing vulnerabilities in widely used software and preparing defenses against them. The company said it expects similar discoveries to increase sharply in coming months.

items._excerpt: Researchers at cybersecurity firm Calif used OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol model to find a critical flaw in PHP. Google-owned security company Wiz independently used Google’s Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI models to identify vulnerabilities in the same core software. PHP maintainers released fixes on Oct. 21 for the two flaws, which had remained hidden for years and could let attackers run code on vulnerable servers without authentication (fortune.com, wiz.io, reuters.com). Wiz said frontier models made a complex exploit chain substantially easier to execute, describing steps that had once been at the edge of what human researchers could achieve (wiz.io). The same capabilities could help attackers adapt exploits to different PHP versions and server configurations, the company warned (techcrunch.com, axios.com). OpenAI said it believes researchers found the flaws before attackers did. It is proposing a repeatable process for identifying and fixing vulnerabilities in widely used software and preparing defenses against them. The company said it expects similar discoveries to increase sharply in coming months (openai.com). Vulnerability surge: A graph compiled by research nonprofit Epoch AI showed significant vulnerabilities reported by major technology companies and open-source projects rising from a few dozen in some months several years ago to about 600 in a typical month (motherjones.com). OpenAI funding: OpenAI pledged $1 billion in subsidized Daybreak access for frontline defenders, with a focus on organizations that have limited security resources (openai.com). Exposure checker: OpenAI published a PHP version-checking tool as a Codex skill to help operators identify potentially vulnerable installations and determine relevant updates (openai.com). Proof-of-concept video: An accidentally posted video showed an exploit working against multiple targets; copies spread online and contributed to faster development and circulation of exploit demonstrations (simonwillison.net).

items.content_html:
🌾 ✏️
